title: Treasury Schedule of Early Withdrawal Penalties on Certificates of Deposit
content:
The penalty a tier of the Certificates of Deposit line publishes is quoted as a number of days of simple interest.

## Schedule

| Tier | Days of interest published as the early withdrawal penalty | Smallest penalty, in days, on principal taken out within six calendar days of funding | Days after funding after which a full withdrawal carries no penalty | Rate the penalty is worked out at | Penalty may reach principal |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6-Month Certificate | 90 | 7 | not offered | the interest rate the certificate carries | yes |
| 11-Month No-Penalty Certificate | 0 | 7 | 6 | the interest rate the certificate carries | yes |
| 12-Month Certificate | 90 | 7 | not offered | the interest rate the certificate carries | yes |
| 18-Month Bump-Up Certificate | 180 | 7 | not offered | the interest rate the certificate carries | yes |
| 36-Month Certificate | 180 | 7 | not offered | the interest rate the certificate carries | yes |
| 60-Month Certificate | 365 | 7 | not offered | the interest rate the certificate carries | yes |

## Waiver after death or incompetence

| Tier | Penalty waived after the owner's death or court-adjudicated incompetence |
|---|---|
| 6-Month Certificate | yes |
| 11-Month No-Penalty Certificate | yes |
| 12-Month Certificate | yes |
| 18-Month Bump-Up Certificate | yes |
| 36-Month Certificate | yes |
| 60-Month Certificate | yes |

## Footnotes to the schedule

The 11-Month No-Penalty Certificate publishes 0 days as its ordinary penalty and is the only tier on this schedule that offers a waiting period after which a full withdrawal carries no penalty at all; that period is 6 days from funding. Its column for the opening days still reads 7, so the two figures are not the same rule: one is the tier's ordinary published penalty, the other the smallest penalty in the first days after funding.

Because every tier permits the penalty to reach principal, an owner who takes money out early may receive less than they placed. A certificate on which little interest has yet been credited is precisely the case in which this bites.
